candidate.title: scChIP-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle scChIP-Seq row of the assigned Illumina schematic: DNA-protein complex → crosslinking → fragmentation → exonuclease digestion → immunoprecipitation → extracted DNA. The leftmost chromatin illustration and caption “Single cell chromatin immunoprecipitation (scChIP-seq)” expand the assay name and do not depict a second workflow branch. Its yellow-highlighted DNA segment has no defined chemical modification or end-group meaning in this crop. The neighboring scRC-Seq and scATAC-Seq rows are outside scope. This is a chromatin-enrichment component schematic ending at DNA, not a complete single-cell library architecture. The verified listed Rotem et al. citation identifies a native droplet-barcoded implementation of scChIP-Seq, called Drop-ChIP in the paper; it resolves how that paper preserves cell identity but does not validate the drawn crosslinking/exonuclease sequence. No additional named workflow is introduced.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operations belong to the row explicitly labeled scChIP-Seq at the declared schematic scope. No alternative branch is shown. Applicability is to this source depiction, not to every implementation of scChIP-Seq. The supplied paper supports a different native, droplet-indexed implementation and the shared purpose of antibody enrichment and DNA readout; its unshown compartment, barcoding and pooling operations are explanatory paper context, not extra graph nodes or preparation history for these drawn local operations. For the paper-supported implementation, reads of the genomic insert locate enriched nucleosomal DNA, while cell and sample indices retain its origin. The paper reports sparse single-cell chromatin profiles, so this readout does not comprehensively enumerate all marked loci. These barcode and sampling claims concern the paper implementation and are not assigned to the unindexed terminal DNA icon.

Use the verified citation to identify the paper-supported native implementation of the named assay and as evidence for its cell-indexing/readout interface; retain the drawn route at schematic scope.
